evaluations.brief_justification: Fails C1, C3, C4, C5, C8. Contains fatal wrong claim that remaining labels are forced when multiple legal assignments remain open after limited observations. Final answer of 2 is far below correct minimum of 15.

Fails C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C8. Lacks a concrete, branch-by-branch strategy with specific label-fixing rules; hand-wavy synthesis claims 'enough information' without showing how different observations resolve to unique assignments.

Fails C4 only. Correctly states 15 and gives valid upper bound proof (1+14 strategy with 7/13 split reasoning), but lacks true lower bound proof. Minimality asserted from arithmetic of its own strategy rather than indistinguishable-case reasoning ruling out ALL strategies with fewer inspections.
Fails C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C8. Claims 1 inspection suffices with 'remaining labels cycle uniquely' - mathematically false as derangements over 3 envelopes have 2 possibilities, not unique assignment.
Fails C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C8. Oscillates among 2, 3, 14, 15 inspections; analysis shows awareness that 15 needed but final answer claims 3, creating internal contradiction.

Fails C1, C3, C4, C5, C6, C8. Claims 3 inspections suffice by inferring pure type from single observation per envelope. Invalid: mixed envelope (7/13 split) could return majority type, making one draw insufficient to prove purity.

Fails C1, C4, C8. Derives correct 14-draw verification rule but double-counts preliminary inspection. States 16 (1+1+14) instead of correct 15; claims 16 is minimum. Strategy is structurally sound but miscounted.

Fails C1, C3, C4, C5, C6, C8. Claims 4 inspections by inspecting one from each envelope with 'assignment follows directly.' Fails worst-case analysis: mixed envelope can return majority type on first draw, making it indistinguishable from pure envelope with single observation.

summary: Audit complete: All 8 candidate solutions were rejected. None satisfied all 8 calibration criteria (C1-C8). Response_C came closest (passing 7/8 criteria: C1-C3, C5-C8) but failed C4 due to insufficient lower bound proof lacking true indistinguishable-case reasoning. The correct minimum is 15 inspections (1 from Mixed-labeled envelope to identify pure type X, 14 from X-labeled envelope to distinguish pure from mixed since mixed has max 13 of any type, plus 2 by elimination).
